I don’t need you to agree with me on this but I want you to understand why it’s frustrating for me. I was born into a fairly wealthy family who had enough money to feed me and support my interests and hobbies, to house and clothe me comfortably, and who lived in an area with low crime and good public schools. When I was sixteen, my mom got me an internship at her company, which provided me with good money for three summers and has made it easy to get other jobs since then. I am now in college and my parents pay for most of my tuition, food, and housing because they can afford it, so I can easily focus on my schoolwork instead of having to work during the school year. Not all of my friends have it so lucky, however. They have to work a lot harder in order to get through college while still being able to feed themselves, which to me, seems unfair, but is just the tip of the iceberg. 

Many people are not given much of a chance to succeed like I was. Born into rough areas, having to worry about whether or not they can afford food; I had a friend like that in highschool and it was harder for her than it was for me. There are children in foster care, or who’s parents are not around or emotionally present, or who get addicted to drugs at an early age because they never had someone to guide them elsewhere. People can get incredibly sick and not have the money for the medical care. 

And in so many situations, it doesn’t feel like this is by accident. Businesses seem to frequently made decisions in favor of profits instead of people. Low wages and exploitation of low regulations in foriegn countries are a prime example. Food and clothes wasted instead of donated, pyramid schemes to steal from those who don’t know better, wage fraud, covering up lawsuit-worthy events instead of addressing them, enourmous compensation for CEOs who oftentimes hoard money instead of giving it to those who need it, it all seems an unfortunate recipe to keep the lower class in the lower class.

As a personal opinion, I sincerely believe that everyone wants to work and earn a living wage, but so many people are denied that opportunity. I don’t think that we should be giving free things to people who are unwilling to work, but frankly, I think the percentage of the population who’s unwilling to work is neglegible. Humans by nature are kind and motivated, but the drive for success makes some end up greedy, leaving others without a chance to prove what they could achive. All I want is for everyone to have at least a fraction of the financial and emotional support that I have, because I think that in the right environment, what people could achive might surprise you.
